items.question: Where will Cal Hacks 13.0 take place?
items.answer: Cal Hacks 13.0 will take place in-person at the Palace of Fine Arts in San Francisco, CA.

items.question: Can I check in late?
items.answer: Yes! We will have check in available throughout the event at the information desk until Sunday.

items.question: How big can teams be?
items.answer: Teams can be anywhere between 1-4 people.

items.question: Can I change teams?
items.answer: Until project submission, you can change teams or make new ones, it's all up to you!

items.question: How do I find teammates?
items.answer: If you don't already have a team, we've setup a #team-formation channel in the slack to introduce yourself & what you might wanna build. Followup in threads for people that you might be interested in working with! We'll also have a team formation activity at the start of the hackathon if you don't find a team in time.

items.question: Will there be food or swag?
items.answer: Yes!! You can pick up swag and food throughout this weekend. Please note that due to limited quantities, each hacker will be limited to only one (1) quantity of each food or swag item distributed. All items will be first-come first-serve. Please bring your hacker code so that we can check you off.

items.question: I need help with my project. Who can I go to for help?
items.answer: Head to the #ask-mentors channel on Slack for help, or visit the Mentor Tables in-person across from the Robotics Space. We have a huge team of mentors available in-person that are excited to help you out with your project, whether it be ideating or debugging!

items.question: Where can I find a list of all the workshops and entertainment options being hosted?
items.answer: Check out hive.hackberkeley.org for our full schedule of events this weekend! We'll have a variety of workshops for you this weekend ranging from student organizations to company sponsors. We'll also have in-person entertainment and games available for you during the event!

items.question: Do you have in-person space available for teams to hack in?
items.answer: Yes! We will have hacking space available in the main area and upstairs on the mezannine

items.question: Do you have in-person space available for hackers to sleep?
items.answer: Yes! We will have a large room away from the main hacking area dedicated as a quiet Sleeping Area for hackers to sleep during the event. We will also have air mattresses that you can rent which are available first-come first-served. We recommend you bring your own sleeping bag/blanket and sleeping pad.

items.question: What are the guidelines for project submission?
items.answer: All submissions must include a 2-3 sentence elevator pitch / summary, team location (your table number), and the team name. Judges will be going around to your table to see what you've made (e.g. a demo!)  and listen to your presentation. All presentations must be 5 minutes or under, as judges only have 5 minutes to spend at a table before they have to go to the next one.

items.question: Where do I submit my project?
items.answer: Submit your hack to a Devpost that we'll be releasing soon! You'll just need to enter your team name, team location (your table number), and a 2 - 3 sentence elevator pitch / summary of your project.

items.question: Can I submit a project that I've worked on previously or submitted to another hackathon?
items.answer: No, you cannot submit a project that has been previously worked on or submitted to another hackathon. Ideation of a project is okay before the hackathon, but all implementation must occur during the hacking period. We have strict measures in place to detect cheating or prior work, and any violations will result in disqualification from receiving a prize.

items.question: Is there any available judging criteria for our projects?
items.answer: Projects will be judged based on impact, functionality, technical complexity, and creativity.

items.question: When will winners be announced?
items.answer: Winners will be announced at our closing ceremony taking place Sunday afternoon

items.question: What is considered a beginner team for the Best Beginner Hack?
items.answer: All members of the team must have attended 0 prior hackathons.
